- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

I now have a comprehensive understanding of the API surface. Here is my report:

---

## API Surface Analysis for `usememos/memos`

**This repository does NOT use GraphQL.** There are zero `.graphql` or `.gql` schema files, no GraphQL-related dependencies in either `go.mod` or `web/package.json`, and no GraphQL configuration anywhere.

### The public API uses gRPC / Connect RPC / gRPC-Gateway (REST transcoding)

The API is defined using **Protocol Buffers (protobuf)** and exposed through three complementary protocols, all derived from the same `.proto` definitions:

**1. Protobuf service definitions** (`/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`):
- `memo_service.proto` -- CRUD for memos, attachments, relations, reactions, comments
- `user_service.proto` -- user management, settings, access tokens, stats
- `auth_service.proto` -- authentication (sign-in, sign-up, token refresh)
- `attachment_service.proto` -- file/attachment management
- `instance_service.proto` -- instance-level settings and configuration
- `ai_service.proto` -- AI features
- `idp_service.proto` -- identity provider (SSO) management
- `shortcut_service.proto` -- URL shortcuts
- `common.proto` -- shared types

Each service method has `google.api.http` annotations providing RESTful HTTP mappings (e.g., `GET /api/v1/memos`, `POST /api/v1/memos`, `PATCH /api/v1/{memo.name=memos/*}`).

**2. Three transport layers registered in** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`:

- **gRPC-Gateway** (REST/JSON over HTTP): Registered at `/api/v1/*` and `/file/*` via `grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2`. This transcodes the protobuf services into a standard REST API based on the `google.api.http` annotations in the `.proto` files. This is what external/third-party HTTP clients would typically consume.

- **Connect RPC**: Registered at `/memos.api.v1.*` via `connectrpc.com/connect`. This is the protocol used by the web frontend (see `@connectrpc/connect` and `@connectrpc/connect-web` dependencies in `web/package.json`, and the client setup in `/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts`). Connect supports both the Connect protocol and gRPC-Web over HTTP/1.1.

- **Native gRPC**: The service structs embed the `Unimplemented*Server` types from the generated gRPC code (visible in `v1.go`), meaning they are full gRPC service implementations. However, the current server startup in `/bench/repo/server/server.go` only serves HTTP (Echo + gRPC-Gateway + Connect), with no separate gRPC listener.

**3. Code generation** (`/bench/repo/proto/buf.gen.yaml`):
- Go protobuf + gRPC stubs (`buf.build/protocolbuffers/go`, `buf.build/grpc/go`)
- Connect RPC Go handlers (`buf.build/connectrpc/go`)
- gRPC-Gateway REST handlers (`buf.build/grpc-ecosystem/gateway`)
- OpenAPI spec generation (`buf.build/community/google-gnostic-openapi`)
- TypeScript/ES client types for the web frontend (`buf.build/bufbuild/es` into `web/src/types/proto`)

**4. Additional non-API routes** registered in `/bench/repo/server/server.go`:
- `/healthz` -- simple health check endpoint (plain Echo handler)
- RSS feed routes via `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/`
- File server routes via `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/`
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) routes via `/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/`
- SSE (Server-Sent Events) endpoint for real-time updates

### Key dependencies

**Go (`go.mod`)**:
- `connectrpc.com/connect v1.19.2` -- Connect RPC framework
- `github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2 v2.29.0` -- REST transcoding
- `google.golang.org/grpc v1.80.0` -- gRPC
- `google.golang.org/protobuf v1.36.11` -- protobuf runtime
- `github.com/labstack/echo/v5` -- HTTP router/framework

**Web frontend (`web/package.json`)**:
- `@connectrpc/connect` and `@connectrpc/connect-web` -- Connect RPC client
- `@bufbuild/protobuf` -- protobuf runtime for TypeScript

### Summary

The API is **protobuf-first** with REST transcoding. There is no GraphQL anywhere. The architecture is:
- Proto definitions define the API contract
- gRPC-Gateway provides a REST/JSON API at `/api/v1/*` (for external consumers)
- Connect RPC provides a binary protocol at `/memos.api.v1.*` (used by the built-in web frontend)
- Both share the same Go service implementations

There is no GraphQL schema in this repository. The premise is incorrect — the public API is not defined in GraphQL at all.

The API is defined using **Protocol Buffer (`.proto`) service definitions** in `proto/api/v1/`, with files such as `memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, and others. Each service method carries `google.api.http` annotations that map RPCs to RESTful HTTP endpoints.

The actual API surface is exposed via three transports, all generated from those same `.proto` files:

1. **gRPC-Gateway (REST/JSON)** — registered at `/api/v1/*` in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, providing a conventional REST API for external consumers.
2. **Connect RPC** — registered at `/memos.api.v1.*` in the same file, used by the built-in web frontend (via `@connectrpc/connect-web`).
3. **gRPC stubs** — generated but not served on a separate listener; the service structs embed the `Unimplemented*Server` types.

Code generation is configured in `proto/buf.gen.yaml`, which drives Go gRPC stubs, Connect handlers, gRPC-Gateway REST handlers, OpenAPI spec generation, and TypeScript client types (output to `web/src/types/proto`).
